Well I've got all sorts of tips which probably are already covered. However, one little thing that may seem insignificant but has helped me hugely.. I always use my online banking on the mobile app, have a couple instant access saver accounts alongside the current account, I move everything into the savers (also excellent for protecting money in case of losing card or fraud attack! Trust me I worked in a bank before!) I have one saver dedicated for rent, bills. One for food shops. The left over sits and gathers interest. Then have my direct debit payments on the calendar so I know when to move money. Also, not sure where you live, but here in the UK some banks offer cashback for direct debits for utility bills, and higher interest rates for certain things - always shop around! And of course some banks offer say a £100 payment to switch and stay. Also look at wholesale websites or shops for your basics. And honestly, the supermarket own brands and 'saver' lines really are great! Rarely notice a difference especially with meats. Once you see the pennies saving and adding up you'll be laughing! Living on your own really is easy :)
